# Local AI over MCP (open-weight model on your CPU) + Multi-engine

> **Status: ✅ proven 2026-11-22.** The steps below were run end to end; the [Proof](#proof) section has the result.

Make a short vertical reel with scenes from all four engines, driven by Local AI over MCP.
Matrix and other combinations: [tutorials README](../README.md).

## Prerequisites

- A running RenderWeld and an API key with the `read,write,render` scopes (step 1).
- A licence key for a real install (the Personal licence is free), or `RENDERWELD_LICENCE_MODE=off` from a checkout for local development only.
- Node.js 22, about 3 GB of disk for the model and 4 GB of free RAM; no GPU needed (a GPU makes it faster).

## Steps

### 1. Start the studio

Pick one. Both serve REST on `http://127.0.0.1:4321/v1` and MCP on `http://127.0.0.1:4321/mcp`.

**A. Docker (release image, needs a licence key).** The Personal licence is
free (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, claimed with a BuildBase account on the
RenderWeld store); commercial use needs a commercial licence.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/buildbase-app/reelforge-studio && cd reelforge-studio
export REELFORGE_SECRET_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)       # keep a copy: it encrypts stored secrets
docker compose up -d --build                                 # 127.0.0.1:4321, hardened defaults
docker compose exec reelforge renderweld licence activate <YOUR-LICENCE-KEY>
docker compose exec reelforge renderweld keys create --name agent --scopes read,write,render
```

**B. From a checkout with pnpm (local development only).** `pnpm dev` sets
`RENDERWELD_LICENCE_MODE=off`, which skips the licence check. That is for
developing on your own machine only, never for a real install; the release
image does not allow it.

```bash
pnpm install
export RENDERWELD_CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chrome-headless-shell   # Chrome Headless Shell for every engine
pnpm keys:create --name agent --scopes read,write,render       # prints rf_... once
pnpm dev
```

Keep the printed key in an environment variable, not in files you commit:

```bash
export RF=http://127.0.0.1:4321
export REELFORGE_API_KEY=rf_...      # the key printed above
export KEY=$REELFORGE_API_KEY
```

More: [DEPLOY.md](../../DEPLOY.md), [CONFIG.md](../../CONFIG.md), [licence](../../DEPLOY.md#licence).

### 2. Install the local model runtime and a model

[node-llama-cpp](https://node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai) runs GGUF models in Node on
the CPU (prebuilt binaries from npm, no compiler). The tested model is
Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, 4-bit (Q4_K_M, 2.5 GB, Apache-2.0); it needs about
4 GB of free RAM with the agent's 4k context. Expect minutes per step on a CPU: the
proof runs on a shared 4-core machine took 4 to 50 minutes per reel, most of it
for writing the manifest. Keep both outside the studio checkout:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/reelforge-local-ai && cd ~/reelforge-local-ai && npm init -y
npm i node-llama-cpp@3.22.3 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2
curl -L --fail -o Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf
```

The download comes from `huggingface.co` and its CDN; behind a strict egress
proxy allow those hosts first.

### 3. Run the local agent

[`scripts/tutorials/local-agent.mjs`](../../../scripts/tutorials/local-agent.mjs)
is the whole agent: the MCP SDK client lists the studio's tools, offers the
model a small subset (`list_templates`, `create_project`, `validate_project`,
`update_scene`, `render_project`, `get_job`, `get_render_output`),
turns each tool's JSON Schema into a grammar so the model can only produce
well-formed arguments, and loops until `get_render_output` has returned a
render (or 25 tool calls are used). Two things it does for small models: a
call the model writes as text (a pretty-printed `<tool_call>` block) is run
like a native one, and when the history outgrows the 4k context the session
restarts from the prompt plus a one-line recap of the progress.

The exact prompt:

```text
You are connected to a ReelForge video studio through the "reelforge" MCP server. Make a vertical reel (1080x1920, 30 fps) about how one reel can mix four render engines: a 9-second reel with four scenes in this order: remotion (kinetic-title, 2 s), motion-canvas (animated-explainer, 3 s), html (html-title, 2 s), hyperframes (hyperframes-title, 2 s). Use the project id "tut-local-ai-multi-engine". Check list_templates for the props, create the project, validate it, render it, call get_job with waitSeconds 45 until the job succeeds, then call get_render_output. Reply with the project id, job id, render id, duration and frame count. Use only the reelforge tools.
```

```bash
REELFORGE_URL=$RF REELFORGE_API_KEY=$KEY \
LOCAL_AGENT_MODULES=~/reelforge-local-ai \
LOCAL_AGENT_MODEL=~/reelforge-local-ai/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  node scripts/tutorials/local-agent.mjs "$(cat prompt.txt)"
```

With **Ollama** or **llama.cpp's `llama-server --jinja`** instead (any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling; **documented, not proven**):

```bash
LOCAL_AGENT_BACKEND=openai LOCAL_AGENT_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 LOCAL_AGENT_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b-instruct \
REELFORGE_URL=$RF REELFORGE_API_KEY=$KEY node scripts/tutorials/local-agent.mjs "$(cat prompt.txt)"
```

### 4. Download and check the reel

```bash
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -o reel.mp4 "$RF/v1/renders/<renderId>/output"
ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 \
  -show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,nb_read_frames:format=duration -of compact reel.mp4
```

## What the agent does

The local model gets the prompt and the tool subset; the agent loop executes every tool call it makes and feeds the result back:

1. `list_templates`
2. `create_project`
3. `validate_project`
4. `render_project`
5. `get_job (repeated)`
6. `get_render_output`

The proof run's actual calls are listed under [Proof](#proof).

## Expected output

- A job that ends `succeeded`, and a render with `final.mp4`, `poster.png` and `render-manifest.json`.
- `final.mp4`: H.264 1080x1920 at 30 fps, 6 to 12 s (the agent picks the timing within the brief; the frame count matches the duration), with an AAC track (silent: no music was set).
- Scenes: one per engine, in the order remotion → motion-canvas → html → hyperframes.
- Texts: written by the agent about the topic in the prompt, so they differ from run to run.

Multi-engine: every scene is rendered by its own engine at the same size and frame rate, then joined with hard cuts to the frame. Each scene keeps its template's duration range (Remotion at most 8 s, Motion Canvas at least 2 s).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `401 unauthorized` | Missing or wrong key. Send `Authorization: Bearer rf_...`; check it with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" $RF/v1/capabilities`. |
| `403 forbidden_host` on `/mcp` | The Host header is not allowed (DNS-rebinding protection). Use `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`, or set `REELFORGE_PUBLIC_URL` / `REELFORGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. |
| `403 licence_required` / `licence_invalid` on a render | Activate a licence key (`renderweld licence activate <key>`; Personal is free). `RENDERWELD_LICENCE_MODE=off` exists for local development from a checkout only. |
| `403 forbidden` (scope) | The key lacks a scope: rendering needs `render`, creating projects `write`. Create a key with `--scopes read,write,render`. |
| An engine shows `available: false` | `RENDERWELD_CHROMIUM_PATH` is unset or wrong (checkout), or the image is not the release image. `get_capabilities` says how to fix it. |
| `invalid_manifest` | `details.issues` lists every problem with its path, e.g. `scenes.1.props.headline`. Fix all and send again. |
| The job stays `running` for minutes | Rendering is CPU-bound; one 8 s reel took 35 to 120 s on a shared 4-core machine. Wait with `get_job` `waitSeconds: 45` (or `?wait=50`); `get_job_logs` shows the stage. |
| `render_failed` with a timeout on an html or hyperframes scene | One scene ran past `render.sceneTimeoutSeconds` (default 900 s). On a slow machine raise `RENDERWELD_RENDER_SCENE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. |
| html, hyperframes or motion-canvas renders fail in Docker | The container needs the seccomp profile `deployment/seccomp/chrome.json` for Chromium's sandbox (`docker compose` sets it); see [DEPLOY.md](../../DEPLOY.md). |
| Very slow first answer | The model reads the system prompt and tool schemas first (a few thousand tokens); on 4 CPU cores that takes a minute or more. Later turns reuse the cache. |
| The model invents template props | It gets the `invalid_manifest` error with every path and usually fixes it in the next call; a bigger model (7B) makes fewer mistakes. |
| `NOT done after 25 tool calls` | Raise `LOCAL_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS`, make the prompt more specific, or use a bigger model. |
| Out of memory | Lower `LOCAL_AGENT_CONTEXT` (e.g. 6144) or use a smaller quantization. |

## Proof

**Passed** (TUT-25 in [TEST_CASES.md](../TEST_CASES.md)).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-11-22 08:44:52 UTC |
| Studio | RenderWeld 0.1.0, commit `47e325e`, started from a checkout with `REELFORGE_LICENCE_MODE=off` (local development only) |
| Reproduce | `pnpm tutorials:prove local-ai multi-engine` |
| Command the proof ran | `node scripts/tutorials/local-agent.mjs "<prompt>"` |
| Model | Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf; 8 turns; 9 tool calls; 2330 s agent time |
| Project / job / render | `tut-local-ai-multi-engine` / `job_mwrmkaet127f21c103` / `run_mwrmkaete3f9d1d76c` |
| Render time | 159.1 s (job start to finish, shared 4-core CPU, one render at a time) |
| Scene engines | remotion, motion-canvas, html, hyperframes |
| ffprobe | 1080x1920, 30 fps, 270 frames (full decode), 9 s, h264 + aac, 681 KB |

Tool calls, in order (9):

1. `list_templates(engine)`
2. `list_templates(engine)`
3. `list_templates(engine)`
4. `list_templates(engine)`
5. `create_project(manifest)`
6. `validate_project(projectId)`
7. `render_project(projectId)`
8. `get_job(jobId, waitSeconds)`
9. `get_render_output(jobId, includePoster)`

The agent's final reply (signed links redacted):

> <tool_call>
> {
>   "name": "render_project",
>   "arguments": {
>     "projectId": "tut-local-ai-multi-engine"
>   }
> }
> </tool_call>

**Note on this proof:** Third attempt. Attempt 1 (2026-11-22 05:11 UTC) failed: the four list_templates results filled the 4k context, and after each reset the loop repeated the whole prompt, so the model created and rendered the project three times and ran out of its 25-call budget (the reel itself rendered correctly). Fix: after a reset with a render job running, the model is only told to finish that job. Attempt 2 was killed by the out-of-memory killer before its first call (shared machine). In this run the context filled once, right after render_project; the model then finished with get_job and get_render_output. The model checked all four templates (three calls in one turn), and writing the four-scene manifest took 6 minutes.
